exposure: Standardized nutrition protocol (trophic feeds, feeding advancement, fortification guidelines, parenteral nutrition concentration parameters, discontinuation of parenteral nutrition and central lines, discontinuation of gastric residual monitoring)
outcome: Days made nil per os (NPO) after feeding initiation
Growth parameters (change in weight, length, head circumference z-score from birth to discharge)
cohort: 136 very low-birth-weight (VLBW) infants, including 77 in the pre-protocol group and 59 in the post-protocol group.
finding: The initiation of a standardized nutrition protocol for VLBW infants significantly improved growth, reduced parenteral nutrition use, and decreased rates of necrotizing enterocolitis, central-line days, cholestasis, and blood transfusions.
